thread:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a subtle latency uptick on the v1.3 canary in us-west1. Token-level breakdown points to repeated kernel swaps around token 16-32. :eyes:
chris: link? dashboard?
mar ia: https://dash.internal/redwood/runtime/perf?panel=token_breakdown&model=v1.3 — look at the orange line for 'kernel_switch_time'.
amit: I ran a quick KV cache check — hit rate dropped ~8% for the canary slice. Might explain the extra fetch + kernel path.
kensuke: did we change batching heuristics for that rollout? I remember we toggled adaptive_slice_threshold last Friday.
maria: yes, we rolled adaptive_slice_threshold=0.6 to reduce tail latency, but the new kernel selector sometimes falls back to a slower quant path when KV misses cluster.
chris: can you paste the PromQL you used for the token-level view?
amit: sure — `sum by (route, model_version) (rate(kernel_switch_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) / sum by (route, model_version) (rate(kernel_switch_duration_seconds_count[1m]))`
mar ia: and KV hit-rate query: `sum(kv_cache_hits_total{model=~"v1.*"}) / sum(kv_cache_requests_total{model=~"v1.*"})`
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary v1.3 rolled to 10% in us-west1 at 2026-02-18T14:02Z :rocket:
sre-oncall: seeing small error bump too — `503` up from baseline 0.03% -> 0.09% in the same window. Might be correlated.
devex: are we sure it's kernel selection and not a quantized kernel regression? Any profiling traces?
kensuke: I captured a few runtime traces. snippet:
```
[2026-02-18T14:05:23Z] model=v1.3 request_id=abc123 kernel=quant_fast -> kernel=quant_safe switch cost=1.9ms kv_hit=false
[2026-02-18T14:05:24Z] model=v1.3 request_id=abc124 kernel=quant_fast -> kernel=float32_fallback switch cost=3.7ms kv_hit=false
```
maria: exactly — when KV misses, the kernel selector sometimes prefers float32_fallback which is ~3-4ms slower per switch. On small inputs that pushes token p95 over SLO.
amit: hypothesis: adaptive batching decreased batch sizes so KV prefetching effectiveness reduced, increasing miss rate.
chris: action idea: for canary, pin kernel selector policy to prefer quant_fast for compatible ops and restore previous adaptive_slice_threshold. Quick A/B: v1.3-canary-a (adaptive 0.6) vs v1.3-canary-b (adaptive 0.4 + kernel-pin).
sre-oncall: +1 — need quick dashboard panels to compare per-route KPIs (p50/p95 token latency, kv_hit_rate, kernel_switch_count) between the two canaries.
devex: I'll add the panels. Prometheus queries + Grafana vars: route, model_version, canary_group. Expect to be live in ~15m.
chris: also add a flamegraph sample for the worst requests — we need to confirm where time is spent after the switch.
kensuke: capturing flamegraphs now; will attach soon.
mar ia: patch proposal: revert adaptive_slice_threshold to 0.45 for the canary group and apply kernel selector override for model=v1.3 in us-west1 for 30m, then re-evaluate.
amit: agreed. I'll monitor KV hit-rate and per-token latency slices.
sre-oncall: if errors keep rising above 0.1% escalate and rollback.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Patch apply: kernel-selector-override @ v1.3/us-west1 by kensuke — started at 2026-02-18T14:20Z
mar ia: initial 10m observations: kv_hit_rate up ~3%, kernel_switch_count down 12%, p95 token latency improved ~1.6ms.
chris: good signal. keep watching for 30m, then decide whether to include override in rollout.
devex: dashboards updated: panel links -> https://dash.internal/redwood/runtime/compare_canaries?v1=canary-a&v2=canary-b
kensuke: uploaded flamegraphs to the thread: https://artifacts.internal/flame/v1.3/canary-b/trace-0001.svg
amit: flame shows most time spent in `kv_lookup` then `kernel_dispatch` on misses — confirms root cause.
maria: preliminary postmortem notes: causal chain = batching heuristic change -> smaller batches -> KV prefetch less effective -> increased KV misses -> kernel selector fallback to slower kernel -> token-level latency regression in canary.
sre-oncall: next steps: (1) revert heuristic in canary (done), (2) kernel selector temp override (done), (3) run A/B for 1h and collect SLO metrics, (4) add automated guardrail: if kv_hit_rate drops >5% OR kernel_switch_count increases >10% trigger canary rollback.
chris: can someone file a small RFC for a permanent mitigation? Options: better prefetch heuristics, sticky kernel routing when KV miss pattern detected, or more aggressive memcache warming. Put it in eng-runtime RFCs.
kensuke: filing now -> https://rfc.internal/r/110-adaptive-batching-kv-mitigation
mar ia: thanks all — keep alerts on. I'll update this thread with 1h results. :thumbsup:
